title: Compatibility index generator + ephemeral smoke runbook for Terraform module/provider upgrades
creator: Ethan Brooks
description: Create an automated compatibility index and an ephemeral smoke-runbook that validates Terraform module and provider upgrades against our Private (VPC) deployment patterns. The index should map module versions to provider versions and known incompatibilities, produce a machine-readable matrix consumed by CI jobs, and drive a canary smoke test that runs in an ephemeral VPC to validate upgrades before we roll them to staging/dedicated/private customers.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable compatibility matrix (CSV + JSON) is generated nightly and on PRs that change module/provider constraints
CI gating: module/provider version bumps must pass ephemeral smoke-runbook before merge to main
Smoke runbook provisions an ephemeral VPC, runs module apply/destroy with representative example stacks, executes post-upgrade health checks, and reports pass/fail with logs
Matrix includes semantic-version ranges, known blocked versions, and recommended pin decisions for each provider/module pair
Documentation: runbook and matrix ingestion steps added to internal Confluence and linked in PR templates
notes: Motivation: recent incidents where provider minor updates changed resource defaults; need deterministic upgrade path for Private VPC customers
We will not attempt to auto-fix incompatible module code in this ticket — goal is detection and blocking with clear remediation guidance
Plan to reuse the existing infra-ci ephemeral cluster (+ignite runner) to avoid standing infra costs
Scope: terraform root modules used by Private deployments and first-party shared modules (networking, storage, secrets). SaaS-facing modules will be handled later
design_decisions: Represent compatibility as a normalized CSV + JSON that includes fields: module_key, module_version, provider, provider_version_range, status (ok|warn|blocked), last_tested
Matrix generator will parse module constraint blocks and call the Terraform Registry / provider release feeds to fill gaps
Use a canary strategy: run smoke tests against the highest-stability permutation first; if failures, run bisect job to narrow to specific provider minor versions
PR blocking implemented via GitHub Action that downloads matrix and runs targeted smoke subset; fail fast to reduce CI cost
implementation_todos: Build matrix generator lambda (python) that scans modules in monorepo and external module manifests
Add GitHub Action 'compat-matrix-check' to PR template
Create ephemeral smoke-runbook Terraform templates (vpc-demo, core-services-demo) and health probes
Wire test results into Slack #infra-upgrades and create a dashboard in Grafana for historical records
Add remediation link generation: for blocked pairs produce suggested pin (e.g., azurerm = "~>3.5.0") and linked GH PR template
testing_plan: Nightly full-matrix run against latest stable provider versions; PR-triggered quick-check that validates only changed module/provider pairs. Smoke tests validate: terraform init/apply/destroy, service-level probes (API ping, DB connection), RBAC and KMS access tests. Failures capture logs + statefiles to S3 for triage.
rollback_plan: If a staged rollout (dedicated/private) observes regressions, operators flip a 'compat-fallback' routing policy to prior module/provider pin combination and open ENG rollback ticket. Matrix generator will mark the failing permutation as 'blocked' and annotate the last known-good version.
risk_summary: False negatives (matrix reporting ok when subtle behavior changed) are highest risk. Mitigation: include functional probes that exercise default resource behaviors; keep windowed canaries for customers on Dedicated who opt into early upgrades.
